memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father. The older daughter had a son, and she named him Moab; he is the father of the Moabites of today. The younger daughter also had a son, and she named him Ben-Ammi; he is the father of the Ammonites of today. - Gen 19:34-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends in shame - two sons born of a sinful act, becoming the fathers of the Moabites and Ammonites, nations that would often oppose Israel in the years to come. It is a bleak conclusion to a bleak chapter. Sin has borne its bitter fruit, and the consequences will echo through generations. Scripture is honest to the very end about the wreckage that compromise leaves behind.

And yet - hold on to hope, because God's grace runs deeper than any mess. Fast forward many centuries, and a Moabite woman named Ruth would leave her people, embrace the God of Israel, and become the great-grandmother of King David (Ruth 4:17). And from David's line would come Jesus Christ Himself. God wove even the Moabites - born from this dark episode - into the family tree of the Saviour of the world.

Think of what this means. From the wreckage of Genesis 19, through a shameful act in a cave, God brought a line that would eventually lead to the Messiah. Grace reached right into the mess and drew out redemption. Nothing is too broken for God to redeem.

This is the hope of the gospel. Your family's failures, the sins of the past, the wreckage you may feel you have inherited or caused - none of it is beyond the reach of God's redeeming grace. He specialises in bringing beauty from ashes, weaving even our darkest chapters into His good purposes. In Christ, the mess is never the final word. Grace is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God's grace can reach into even the worst mess?
- How does it encourage you that God brought the Messiah's line through such brokenness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that Your grace reaches into even the darkest mess and brings redemption. Thank You that from this broken story You brought the line of the Saviour. Redeem my brokenness too, for Your glory.
Amen.
